primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1382852/ (all 60 printed pages A181–A240; A235 presentation 2001 gallstones and 2006 hypertensive LES; A207 presentations 1764–1765)
assessment: The complete 1995 UEG Gut Part IV scans include an olive-oil use row in Misciagna et al. 2001 on A235. It is a dietary covariate in a gallstone-incidence cohort, and it loses significance after accounting for other associated variables. On the same printed page, 2006 assesses dysphagia during oral nifedipine treatment for hypertensive lower oesophageal sphincter. A207 1764 treats Parkinson gastrointestinal symptoms with domperidone, while 1765 concerns dysphagia with hemiparesis. These are distinct presentations and provide no extra-virgin olive-oil comparison for Parkinson swallowing.
